map.text: The roof of the board, right under Topus. Living stone, deep mines, and a Tower nobody else is allowed to find.

map.name: The Clockwork Heights
map.text: Where progress climbs toward the sky: parade grounds, signal towers, and the garden where the world’s clock is wound.

map.name: The Wildwood
map.text: The old forest down Levt’s side of the board, with castles at its edges and foothills behind it. Tradition grows here, slowly.

map.name: Middlemark
map.text: The intersection: the middle ground, the meeting and the conflict of every extreme. A city built over the sleeping Gol’God’Oth, with the Temple of the Four Sides at its heart.

map.name: The Works
map.text: Rightorious’s side of the board, all chimneys and workshops. Everything new in Teece is built, tested and blown up here first.

map.name: The Gloaming
map.text: Old, dark and close to the Pit: crumbling castles, open graves and the Hollow where the Witches brew. The Vampires and the Zombies have warred here for ten thousand years.

map.name: The Sinking Sands
map.text: Directly over the Pit, slowly sliding into it. Ankhtepot’s tombs, the Brood Mother’s silk, and the market where gods are rented by the hour.

map.name: The Badlands
map.text: The dark and forgotten refuse of progress, down near the Pit: dust, scrap, blast craters, the drains under the Dump, and everything the Works and Middlemark threw away and stopped thinking about. Some of it stands up and walks. Some of it waits.

map.name: The Pit
map.text: Beneath the bottom edge, past Bottomor. The Devils run it as a business.

map.name: The World of Teece
map.text: Off the board but still Teece: the endless country past the edges, where the world folds over on itself. Things here are not from anywhere in particular.

parts.title: The Summons
parts.intro: Middlemark sleeps soundly as a rule, which in a city built over Gol’God’Oth takes real talent. This season the floor has started to hum. The Priests of the Four Sides say the old thing underneath is turning over in its sleep, and the Cult in the cellars is lighting candles. The Temple has sent its summons to every panel of the board: send your champions to Middlemark. You carry the summons, and in every panel you fight as whoever answers it.
parts.outro: The last line never lights. The Wizards seal the middle panel for the third time, the Host goes home to the Heavens, and the Paladins and the Knights argue about horses all the way back up the board. Under Middlemark, Gol’God’Oth turns over and goes back to sleep. The Common Levy, who were never told how close it was, sleep soundly too.

chapters.title: The Drains
chapters.text: The first sign is the Rats. They are coming up every pipe from the Badlands at once, and the Rat King is not so much leading them as running in front of them. The Common Levy has pitchforks, honest numbers and nothing else. That will do.
chapters.win: The Levy holds the cellars. A cornered Rat says only that the drains under Middlemark have gone warm. You take the summons and leave by Levt’s road, into the Wildwood.

chapters.title: The Old Road
chapters.text: The Wildwood will hear the summons, but not while Ogres from the foothills are using its trees for clubs. They felt the ground hum too, and decided to shove it. The forest is very patient. You are not: feed the plants and let them grow.
chapters.win: The Ogres go home sulking, and the oldest oak in the forest bends to listen. It has felt Gol’God’Oth shift among its roots, and it points you uphill, to the High Mountains, where the stone remembers everything.

chapters.title: Living Stone
chapters.text: The Dwarves will march for Middlemark, but the Rock has just found another of their tunnels running through it and has declined to move until somebody apologises. Nobody is going to apologise. Let the gear do the work.
chapters.win: The Rock grumbles and settles. The Dwarf foreman swears the deepest seam now runs warm, all the way down toward the middle panel. You take the long road down Levt’s side of the board, into the Gloaming.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Years
chapters.text: The Gloaming has no time for summonses. The Vampires and the Zombies have been at war for ten thousand years, and neither side will send a single Teece to Middlemark while the other still stands. The Vampires will hear you out if you win them this round. They grow by taking, so take.
chapters.win: The Zombies fall back to their graves, for now, and an Elder admits the Pit next door has been loud lately: the Devils are writing contracts as if they expect a sale. The Elder sends you north, where the old Light still burns.

chapters.title: Stolen Horses
chapters.text: The Paladins will answer the summons on one condition: their horses back. The Knights ride up from the Wildwood marches on warhorses bred from Celestial Steeds stolen from the Paladins, and they have no intention of walking home. Swear your Oaths and keep them.
chapters.win: The Knights walk home. The Paladins swear to stand at the Temple when the time comes, and their eldest says the Light has seen the Cult’s candles in Middlemark’s cellars. You cross the top of the board and go down Rightorious’s side, to the Works.

chapters.title: Leftovers
chapters.text: Everything the Works throws away ends up in the Dump, and the Dump has started throwing it back. The Garbage once ate a Robot, and the Robots have not forgotten. The Gadgeteers will build what Middlemark needs if the Drones can clear the yard. Copy yourself, and keep copying.
chapters.win: The yard is clear, and the Gadgeteers build a needle that measures how hard a sleeping god is pushing back. It points at the middle panel and trembles. For anything more, you will have to ask the sky.

chapters.title: Seven Against Six
chapters.text: Above the top edge, the Host of Topus has been watching the board. A Devil has climbed all the way up from the Pit to offer it terms: stay out of Middlemark, and the Pit will too. The Host keeps its numbers at seven out of spite for the Devils’ six. Remind them why.
chapters.win: The Devil tears up its contract, which for a Devil is a serious emotional event, and falls back to the Pit. The Host will descend on Middlemark when called, and an Angel tells you who knows how deep Gol’God’Oth really sleeps: the Wizards, in their Tower.

chapters.title: The Locked Library
chapters.text: The Wizards have sealed the middle panel twice and will do it a third time, but their Tower is under siege. The Mad, scholars who listened too closely to the floor of Middlemark, have come for the Eldritch Library the Wizards locked and lost the key to. They throw away everything they hold, and it works. Out-think them.
chapters.win: The Mad scatter, still arguing with the voices. The Wizards find the key in the last place anybody looked and read the one page that matters: tonight the Cult lights its last line. They can seal the middle panel, if the Temple stands until dawn. You go home to Middlemark.

chapters.title: The Temple of the Four Sides
chapters.text: The Cult of Gol’God’Oth has come up out of the cellars with its pentagram nearly lit. Everyone you met is on the way, but the Temple is here and they are not, yet. The Priests stand on top of the oldest thing in Teece and pray to the four Sides that hold the world in its frame. Face your god, and Smite.

parts.title: The Turning
parts.intro: Gol’God’Oth went back to sleep, but it turned over first, and the board has not sat straight since. Panels lean. Ground rises where nobody laid it, the tallest Teece find the floor tilting away under them, and strange things are coming in through the creases at the edge of the world. Everyone who answered the summons has gone home, and whatever you lead now fights uphill: the tilt is printed on every chapter before you fight it.
parts.outro: The Horsemen ride off to announce something else. The Warlocks pay what they owe, with interest, and Gol’God’Oth settles into a sleep deep enough that the floor stops humming. The board sits straight again, more or less. The Common Levy never noticed it had tilted.

chapters.title: Aftershock
chapters.text: The quake cracked the Temple floor, and the middle panel now runs hot with whatever Gol’God’Oth is dreaming: anything standing on it is stronger. Berserkers have come down from the Hallowed North to fight on it, because of course they have. Field Marshal Marshall has drilled the Levy into an Army. Hold the middle.
chapters.win: The Berserkers go home happy, which is how Berserkers lose. The Field Marshal plants a flag on the warm stones and sends you to the edge of the board, where the reports are strangest.

chapters.title: The Creases
chapters.text: At the edge of the board the World of Teece folds over on itself, and since the quake the folds have opened. The Locusts are pouring out of the Wastes and have already sown a Wheat Field in the middle of the board. The only ones in their way are the Noughts and Crosses, who fell out of a crease themselves. The tilt runs their way: everything of theirs comes in a little bigger.
chapters.win: Three in a row, and the crease closes. Something on the far side of it was moving the wrong way, down toward the Badlands.

chapters.title: Dust
chapters.text: The Badlands have turned to dust storms, and two corners of the board are buried under drifts nobody can stand on. The Mimics like it: a chest does not need much room to wait for a hand. The Gun rode in to clear them out, set up a Gun Range in the middle of the dust, and has not stopped explaining how.
chapters.win: The last strongbox goes down full of bullets and gives a little back: a map, in grave dust, of a tomb that is sliding faster than it should.

chapters.title: The Slide
chapters.text: Ankhtepot’s tomb slides an inch a year toward the Pit. Since the quake it has slid a yard, and the bottom of the Sinking Sands has turned to a swamp that holds whatever steps in it. The Brood Mother has spun her Web across the tomb’s door. Ankhtepot refuses to accept this, as he refuses most things.
chapters.win: The silk burns and the tomb stops sliding, mostly. Ankhtepot’s priests say the sand is not sinking any more. It is being pulled, from below.

chapters.title: Below the Books
chapters.text: Something under the Pit is pulling. The Devils say it has nothing to do with them and have a contract to prove it. The Demons, who live further down and read no contracts at all, say the Devils have been selling off the fires, and Hell is already breaking through the bottom corners of the board. In the Pit everything belongs to the Devils, the advantage included.
chapters.win: The Demons drag the books down into Hell and burn them, which turns out to settle the argument. With the paperwork gone, the pull stops. Up in the Clockwork Heights, the world’s clock has started running the wrong way.

chapters.title: Backwards
chapters.text: The quake knocked the world’s clock out of true, and in the Hours everything runs backwards. Zeus’s Stormborn have flashed down to see what the noise is, and they arrive already grown, three up on every side. Every third round the whole field grows back a little more. The Gardeners have kept two Hilltops for you either side of the middle.
chapters.win: The storm blows over and the Gardeners wind the clock forward again. Every tick points down Levt’s side of the board, into the Wildwood.

chapters.title: Fey Weather
chapters.text: The Wildwood has risen into hills overnight, one at each corner of the forest, and the Witches have climbed up out of the Hollow to take them. They want their stolen spells back. The hills make the Witches bigger than ever and the Pixies are as tiny as always, but nobody has ever managed to hit a 1.
chapters.win: The Witches go home without their spells and with several new ones they did not ask for. A Pixie, upside down in a tree, points out what nobody else has: every crease is opening toward the same place.

chapters.title: The Space Between Spaces
chapters.text: The creases meet in the Space Between Spaces, and the Planewalkers have been redecorating it since the quake: two corners have been turned inside out by the Dimension of Change. Everything of theirs comes in bigger than it should. The Fusion Teece were born here, and the middle panel still remembers them. Become one with something, and push them back.
chapters.win: The Planewalkers fold up their ground and the seam narrows. On the far side of it, under the middle of everything, something has stopped dreaming and started to listen.

chapters.title: The Rent

events.where: the four panels around the middle
events.name: Middlemark burns

chapters.text: The Four Horsemen have ridden into Middlemark to announce the end of the world, as they do whenever anything happens, and every second round they set the streets around the Temple alight. This time Gol’God’Oth is listening, and the Warlocks are behind on the rent. Sign with every patron who will have you, and hold the warm middle until the Old One goes back to sleep.

parts.title: The Folded World
parts.intro: The board sits straight again, but the World of Teece past its edges does not. When Gol’God’Oth turned over it creased the far country, and the creases are folding inward: panels from nowhere in particular are being stitched onto the board, the sky has come loose, and the old rules hold a little less every day. The Planewalkers say the World can be folded back, but only from the far side of the last crease. Every fight from here on breaks a rule, and some of them are fought three ways.
parts.outro: The Planewalkers fold the last crease shut, and the World of Teece lies flat again past every edge of the board. The Tendril sinks back into the warm floor. Under Middlemark, Gol’God’Oth sleeps, and for the first time since all this began, it does not dream. The Common Levy, as ever, slept through the whole thing.

chapters.title: Until Dawn
chapters.text: The night came loose when the world folded, and in the Gloaming it has stopped ending. The Vampires have caught the Zombies in the open with every advantage the dark can give, and a Bat Cave in the corner keeps their numbers up. You do not have to win. You have to still be standing when round eight ends, while the night bites everything on the field.
chapters.win: Round eight ends, the sun finds its way back over the edge of the board, and the Vampires go to ground. Nagash’s dead are still standing, more or less. Behind the sunrise, the Badlands are fighting over something new.

chapters.title: The Dump Wars
chapters.text: A fold has dropped a second Dump on top of the first, and everything in the Badlands wants it. The Rats, the Garbage and the Mimics are fighting for every heap at once, three ways, on a board grown to four by four. The Rats have a nest in one corner, and every second round the heaps in the middle catch fire.
chapters.win: The Rat King sits on top of both Dumps and is very pleased about it. From up there he can see what nobody else has: the sky above the board has come unstuck.

chapters.title: Zero Gravity
chapters.text: Up in the Heavens the fold has let go of the sky, and nothing stays down any more: every Teece flies. The Heavens are wide, so taking the field needs a lead of six. The Stormborn are fast and do not care. The Solar orders are patient, know the sky better than anyone, and hold the Solar Terrace in the middle of it.
chapters.win: The sun and the moon settle back into their turning, and things start falling again, mostly where they were. A boulder from the High Mountains misses you by a panel on its way down.

chapters.title: Rockfall
chapters.text: The fold has tipped the High Mountains, and the peaks are coming down. The Bombardiers think this is the best thing that has ever happened to them and have already dug in. At the end of rounds two, four and six a boulder buries another panel for good. The Rock declines to be moved. It may have to decline very hard.
chapters.win: The Bombardiers run out of things to blow up before the Rock runs out of patience. From the top of the rubble you can see down into the Wildwood, where three old feuds have broken out at once.

chapters.title: Three Feuds
chapters.text: The fold has crushed the Wildwood’s foothills together, and the Berserkers, the Ogres and the Army have all woken up next to each other. Each of them has a grudge against at least one of the others. In the fold everything runs fast: every player plays two Teece and draws two cards a turn.
chapters.win: Twelve Berserkers walk out of the forest, which is how many walked in. The Ogres have been shoved and the Army has been told. In Middlemark, meanwhile, the treasure has started to bite.

chapters.title: Outnumbered
chapters.text: Treasure has been turning up all over Middlemark since the fold, and the Knights rode in to claim it. It is Mimics, all of it, and the Rats have come up the drains to share whatever the Mimics leave. You are on your own against both of them, so you fight as two: two Teece and two cards a turn.
chapters.win: The Knights ride out with nothing but their horses, which they regard as a victory. A Mimic, broken open, gives a little back: a letter from the Pit, signed by the Archdevil, inviting the Hallowed North to surrender.

chapters.title: The Giant

field.where: one of the four middle panels

chapters.text: The Archdevil has climbed out of the Pit and up the board to the Hallowed North, and the fold has made it enormous: every Devil fights at +4, and the Archdevil is already standing when the fight begins. The Runeblade tribe has never needed help, and is accepting it anyway. The Wolves run beside you.
chapters.win: The Archdevil goes back down the board in pieces, each of them filing a complaint. The Wolves howl, and the Runeblade tribe pretends not to be moved. In Middlemark, the libraries have started to burn.

chapters.title: The Burning Library
chapters.text: The Wizards came down from their Tower to save the Eldritch Library, and found the Mad already inside and the whole thing burning. Every second round the fire takes every battleground on the field, and every third round the shelves come down on everything. The floor is thin: a lead of three takes the field, for either side.
chapters.win: The Mad walk out of the ashes holding the one book that mattered, which they immediately throw away, because the voices said so. It lands open at a map of the last crease, at the far edge of the world.

chapters.title: The Last Crease

events.where: one of the four middle panels
events.name: Gol’God’Oth reaches

chapters.text: At the last crease the World of Teece folds against itself, and the corners of the board have folded away entirely. Everything from nowhere in particular has come to stop you closing it: the Fusion Teece from the Space Between Spaces, and the Four Horsemen, who have been waiting for exactly this. The Planewalkers treat the ground itself as a weapon, and fight as two; the crease is wide, and taking the field needs a lead of six. Underneath it all, Gol’God’Oth is reaching up.
